clue.text: Enquiry about parent's relations

parts.note: reads as a polite question after someone's dad, but the phrase is also British slang for sexual relations

explanation.definitionFit: A jocular British euphemism for sex is this very question about a person's dad, so it both asks after a parent and means intimate relations.

clue.text: Going to rewrite first curriculum vitae

indicators.note: to rewrite something is to put its letters down again in a new arrangement
first picks out the opening letter of the word curriculum

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to redraft the start of a job applicant's CV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curriculum vitae' looks like one unit, but only the first letter of 'curriculum' joins VITAE before 'rewrite' scrambles CVITAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going, as in a going concern, is functioning or operating, a synonym of busy and working.

clue.text: Paper's colourful coverage of wedding

parts.note: sounds like a newspaper's report on a marriage, but means the bits of coloured paper thrown over the couple

explanation.definitionFit: Tiny pieces of coloured paper are showered over newlyweds, literally covering them at the ceremony.

clue.text: Mean to be like a petty criminal?

definitions.meaning: a small-time thief stealing coins, taking the phrase literally

explanation.definitionFit: Being miserly means hoarding every coin; read literally, the phrase describes a thief who steals only small coins.

clue.text: Ex-serviceman or a keen train spotter, maybe

indicators.note: ex means out of, so the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Is a former soldier the same as an enthusiastic railway watcher?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ex' looks like part of 'Ex-serviceman', but it signals that the answer comes out of 'serviceman or a keen'.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an obsessive hobbyist, the kind stereotyped as standing on platforms noting locomotive numbers in a hooded coat.

clue.text: Bar supporter from football ground

parts.note: sounds like a pub regular who follows a team, but means the upright holding up the crossbar on a pitch

explanation.definitionFit: Each upright at the end of a soccer pitch holds up the crossbar, so it literally supports a bar.

clue.text: Examination previously completed

parts.note: once means at a former time, previously
over means finished, completed

explanation.surface: An exam that was already finished earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick look over something to check it is a brief inspection, an informal examination.

clue.text: Stopped waiting for reply

definitions.meaning: suspended, paused for the time being
kept waiting on a phone line before someone answers

explanation.definitionFit: A project that is paused is suspended, and a caller on the line kept listening to music is also left waiting.

clue.text: A lot of calculation when called to account

definitions.text: A lot of calculation when called to account

parts.words: A lot of calculation when called to account
parts.note: reads as a full day spent doing sums, but means the time of judgement when one must answer for one's deeds

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical judgement day is when everyone must answer for their conduct; read literally it is a whole day of reckoning, or calculating.

clue.text: Manager used to steam trains

indicators.note: used here means put to work in another arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A railway boss who was accustomed to steam locomotives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to' reads as 'formerly', but 'used' is the anagram signal and 'to steam trains' is its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a railway station is its manager.

clue.text: Body is the right size to return for fresh start

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the words for being the right size are read backwards

parts.note: something that fits is the right size

indicators.note: start means the opening letter of the word fresh

explanation.surface: Something that fits properly being sent back so you can begin again.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a corpse, a dead body, from its rigidity.

clue.text: Of course aunt rioted at demonstration

indicators.note: rioted means ran wild, so the letters of aunt are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a rally is a mass political demonstration

explanation.surface: Naturally, Auntie ran riot at the protest march.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean as expected, without question, like obviously or certainly.

clue.text: Teens start popular break- dance

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it apart, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: start means the opening letters of popular

explanation.surface: Youngsters take up a fashionable breakdance.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'start' takes the first two letters of 'popular', PO, and 'break' then rearranges TEENSPO.
explanation.definitionFit: An early twentieth-century ballroom dance in quick march time, one of many named dances.

clue.text: Slough's flying start

definitions.meaning: slough means to shed, as a snake does its skin
the moment an aircraft leaves the ground

explanation.definitionFit: Shedding skin is to remove it, peel it away; an aircraft's departure from the runway is its first moment of flight.

clue.text: Challenge ending with death chamber

parts.note: sounds like an execution, but the chamber is the loaded slot of a revolver's cylinder

explanation.definitionFit: A deadly game of chance in which players spin a revolver with one bullet and fire at their own heads.

clue.text: Support for jockey in prison over press set-up

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: stir is slang for jail

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to spur is to urge or press on

explanation.surface: A rider held in jail over a matter of press set-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal loops hanging from a saddle hold a rider's feet, supporting a horseman.

clue.text: Officer and doctor each held when close to death

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant
as means when, at the time that

indicators.note: each says the same word is held by both officer and doctor

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner
as means when, at the time that

explanation.surface: An army officer and a medic both detained as a patient lies dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each' tells you the same short word for 'when' sits inside both the officer and the doctor, not just one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A final breath is taken at the point of dying; the phrase also means at the very final moment.

clue.text: Angle a half-frame makes with dilapidated hut

indicators.note: half means only the front half of the word for the frame is used

parts.note: a Zimmer frame is a walking frame

indicators.note: dilapidated means falling apart, so the letters of hut are disordered

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle about a broken frame and a run-down shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps ZIM from ZIMMER, a Zimmer being a walking frame for the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy and navigation, the horizontal angle of a bearing measured clockwise from north.

clue.text: Corporate support enjoyed by sporting cups

definitions.text: Corporate support enjoyed by sporting cups

parts.words: Corporate support enjoyed by sporting cups
parts.note: sounds like business sponsorship for sports trophies, but corporate means bodily and the cups are a bra's, lifted by support

explanation.definitionFit: A bra that raises the bust gives lift to its cups; winners also raise a sporting trophy high.

clue.text: Nothing approved after film got it wrong

indicators.note: after places the other pieces following the film word

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass
O is the zero shape for nothing
OK means approved

explanation.surface: A movie that won approval despite being misjudged.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to misjudge or confuse one thing for another, a synonym of erred.

clue.text: Alternatives include a third rate speaker

indicators.note: include means hold within, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: two ors, each word introducing an alternative

indicators.note: third picks the third letter of the word rate

explanation.surface: Options that take in a third-rate public speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gives formal speeches is a public speaker.

clue.text: Unlucky to be taken by negotiator

definitions.text: Unlucky to be taken by negotiator

parts.words: Unlucky to be taken by negotiator
parts.note: an exclamation of sympathy meaning bad luck, and also uncompromising positions a tough bargainer might adopt

explanation.definitionFit: A British expression of commiseration for bad luck; also firm, unyielding policies adopted in talks.

clue.text: God ensnared a little bit

annotationWithheld.why: God ensnared a little bit (5): the only parse, RA in GIN, needs 'ensnared' to give GIN and also signal the insertion, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Wish for no more rotten trickery

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the wish on a gravestone for one who is no more
off means gone bad, as with food

explanation.surface: Hoping for nothing further from bad deceit.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle or fraud is a piece of cheating, deception.

clue.text: Maybe heaped mash on to peas

indicators.note: mash means crush into a pulp, so the letters are pulped and reformed

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction to crush something over peas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mash' looks like the food, but it is the anagram signal for 'on to peas'.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure in cooking recipes is often described as heaped or level, so this is an example.
